title: Assistant Athletic Director, Development
description:
Position Overview

The Assistant Athletic Director/Development position will serve as
a gift officer on behalf of the Athletic Department. This position
will develop and manage a portfolio consisting of mid-major donors,
major gift donors, and prospects. The primary focus will be on
identifying new prospects, cultivating current/prospective donors,
soliciting major gifts, and stewarding existing/new donors. This
position will manage the Athletics Endowment Program and assist
with management of the Butler Way Society.

Responsibilities

Fundraising

Manage a portfolio of approximately 100 donors and prospects
and work towards individual metric goals including visits,
qualification/disqualifications, solicitations, and total dollars
raised.
Identify, prioritize, cultivate and solicit current and new
gift prospects primarily in, but not limited to, the
$10,000-$250,000 range.
Partner with the Office of University Advancement to ensure
compliance with all relevant University and University Advancement
fundraising policies and procedures.
Manage Athletics Endowment Program with expectations of donor
participation and endowment growth.
Assist Senior Associate Athletic Director/Development with all
fundraising initiatives

Events

Attend and have a presence at Athletics Department and Bulldog
Club fundraising events including, but not limited to, Butler
Basketball Tip-Off Party, Butler Way Society events, Corporate Golf
Outing, Butler Golf Classic, Hall of Fame events, and Athletic
Director’s Reception.
Collaborate with Director of Development and Advancement events
team for planning and administration of Athletics Department and
Bulldog Club fundraising event.

Priority Points

Bulldog Club lead for the Priority Points System
Maintain full knowledge and history of the points system and
provide answers and suggestions to any inquiries from
current/prospective donors and season ticket holders.
Work directly with Advancement Services on coordinating all
priority point information and data.
Serve as lead for Advancement staff when they receive questions
about priority points, serving as a resource for all front-line
fundraisers so they have a working knowledge of the priority points
system to better assist University donors/prospects.
Assist the Athletics Ticket Office in annual Select-A-Seat
event

Hospitality

On gamedays, spend time in various hospitality areas (i.e.
Wildman Room, Efroymson Family Gym, Tony’s on 49th, Sellick Room,
and Terrace Tent) effectively using this time to cultivate
relationships with those donors/prospects in attendance.

Donor Relations

Cultivation and stewardship; attend away games and associated
events (when applicable) to further relationships with assigned
donors and prospects.
Full understanding of the university’s alumni, donor, and
prospective donor database with the ability look-up data on
specific donors, run lists of gifts and data, as well as input
contact reports.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
3-5 years successful fundraising related (sales)
experience
Knowledge and understanding of philanthropy and fundraising
principles
Organizational skills; ability to multi-task/manage several
projects simultaneously and meet deadlines
Demonstrated flexibility, creativity, strategic-thinking
skills; willingness to take initiative and learn
Experience working in intercollegiate, higher education, or
non-profit fundraising
Ability to communicate with donors and internal constituents
both written and verbal
Positive attitude with strong interpersonal skills along with
strong customer service skills
Proven ability to work autonomously, collaboratively and within
a team structure
Ability to execute face-to-face solicitations in support of
organization’s mission
Travel related to donor visits and events as needed
Proficiency in software systems such as: MS Word, Office,
Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and fundraising CRM
systems

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree preferred
Experience in an intercollegiate athletic department
preferred

About Us

Butler University is a private, nationally recognized comprehensive
university encompassing seven colleges: Arts, Business,
Communication, Education, Liberal Arts & Sciences, Pharmacy
& Health Sciences and Founder's College. Approximately 4,500
undergraduate and 1,000 graduate and doctoral students are enrolled
at Butler, representing 46 states and 24 countries.

Join us at the crossroads of tradition & transformation. A
career at Butler University offers more than just a job—it’s an
opportunity to join a dedicated, innovative, and supportive
community grounded in equity, academic excellence, and meaningful
impact. Aligned with Boldly Butler, our strategic plan, faculty and
staff play a vital role in delivering transformational learning
experiences, enriching our campus and community, and ensuring a
thriving Butler for generations to come.

Butler University is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome
applications from all individuals, regardless of age, sex, race,
religion, color, disability, protected veteran status, national
origin, or any other legally protected category.
